title: Compatible surjective local maps from a common prime localization
statement: Let $D$ be a commutative ring and let $P,Q,A$ be commutative local rings, each with exactly one maximal ideal, denoted $\mathfrak m_P,\mathfrak m_Q,\mathfrak m_A$. Let $u:P\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $v:Q\twoheadrightarrow A$ be surjective local ring homomorphisms, where local means carrying the maximal ideal into the maximal ideal. Suppose ring maps $f:D\to P$ and $g:D\to Q$ satisfy $u\circ f=v\circ g=:h$. Assume that for every $p\in P$ there exist $a,t\in D$ with $f(t)$ a unit and $p f(t)=f(a)$, and that for every $q\in Q$ there exist $c,z\in D$ with $g(z)$ a unit and $q g(z)=g(c)$. Then $\mathfrak n=h^{-1}(\mathfrak m_A)$ is a prime ideal, and $\mathfrak n=f^{-1}(\mathfrak m_P)=g^{-1}(\mathfrak m_Q)$. Put $T=D_{\mathfrak n}$ with canonical map $\iota:D\to T$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. There are unique ring maps $\alpha:T\to P$, $\beta:T\to Q$, $\gamma:T\to A$ with $\alpha\iota=f$, $\beta\iota=g$, and $\gamma\iota=h$. All three maps are surjective and local, and $u\circ\alpha=\gamma=v\circ\beta$. For $d\in D$ and $t\notin\mathfrak n$ their values are $\alpha(d/t)=f(d)f(t)^{-1}$, $\beta(d/t)=g(d)g(t)^{-1}$, and $\gamma(d/t)=h(d)h(t)^{-1}$. No Noetherian, regularity or completeness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization), existence, uniqueness and formula for the extensions; agent refinement establishing the common prime, locality and surjectivity under unit-denominator hypotheses, abstracted from returned proof steps 2 (last sentence), 3 and 4.

proof.text: For $x\in P$, locality gives $x\in\mathfrak m_P\Rightarrow u(x)\in\mathfrak m_A$. Conversely, if $x\notin\mathfrak m_P$, the unit criterion makes $x$ invertible; applying $u$ to an inverse makes $u(x)$ invertible, hence outside $\mathfrak m_A$. Thus $u^{-1}(\mathfrak m_A)=\mathfrak m_P$. The identical argument with $v$ gives $v^{-1}(\mathfrak m_A)=\mathfrak m_Q$. Taking inverse images along $f$ and $g$ and using $uf=vg=h$ proves both asserted equalities for $\mathfrak n$.

source.place: Tag 00CP (proposition-universal-property-localization), statement and fraction formula; Tag 00E9 (lemma-characterize-local-ring)

proof.text: The maps $u\alpha$ and $\gamma$ agree after precomposition with $\iota$, since $(u\alpha)\iota=uf=h=\gamma\iota$. The uniqueness clause of the universal property therefore gives $u\alpha=\gamma$. Likewise $(v\beta)\iota=vg=h$ gives $v\beta=\gamma$.

For $p\in P$, choose the assumed $a,t\in D$ with $f(t)$ a unit and $p f(t)=f(a)$. The unit criterion and step 1 give $t\notin\mathfrak n$, so $a/t\in T$, and the fraction formula gives $\alpha(a/t)=f(a)f(t)^{-1}=p$. For $q\in Q$, choose $c,z$ with $g(z)$ a unit and $qg(z)=g(c)$; again $z\notin\mathfrak n$ and $\beta(c/z)=q$. Thus $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are surjective. For $b\in A$, surjectivity of $u$ supplies $p$ with $u(p)=b$; the preceding construction supplies $w\in T$ with $\alpha(w)=p$, hence $\gamma(w)=u\alpha(w)=b$.

source.place: Agent fraction-preimage argument using Tag 00CP and Tag 00E9

proof.text: The prime-localization definition says that $T$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak nT$, the ideal generated by the elements $\iota(a)$ for $a\in\mathfrak n$. For each such generator, step 1 gives $\alpha(\iota(a))=f(a)\in\mathfrak m_P$ and $\beta(\iota(a))=g(a)\in\mathfrak m_Q$, while $\gamma(\iota(a))=h(a)\in\mathfrak m_A$ by definition. Every element of $\mathfrak nT$ is a finite sum $\sum_i w_i\iota(a_i)$; its image under each map is the corresponding sum of multiples of elements of the target maximal ideal. Hence each image lies in that maximal ideal. This proves locality of all three maps.
